newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -- High run rates give API data bearish tone.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -- High run rates give API data bearish tone.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 06/20/97 WEEK ENDED 06/20/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 2.25 112,625 UP 0.905 MLN
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.50 97.6 UNCHD PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
(STOCKS IN THOUSANDS/BBLS, CHANGES IN MLN/BBLS)
Traders digested this week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) with mild but unmistakable bearishness after the report showed that U.S. refineries are still running like gangbusters.
"As long as we continue to be running at these levels, it's going to be hard to get bullish," said Tom Bentz, energy analyst at High Yield Analytics in New York.
Crude stocks fell by 756,000 barrels to 322.3 million, helped by a relative lull in imports which fell to 8.25 million barrels per day (bpd) from just over 10 million bpd in the previous report.

But concerns that high refinery run rates, at 97.6 percent of capacity for the second week in a row, could flood the market with gasoline were tempered by views that demand has been good enough to prevent that.
Implied demand was pegged at 8.75 million barrels per day, an appetite so ravenous that analysts said it helped offset high import levels of 583,000 bpd for the week.
According to the API, gasoline stocks rose last week by 592,000 barrel to 205.5 barrels.
But, dealers were divided as to whether this would be one of the last builds of the season.
"This could be one of the last builds before we start to see seasonal declines," said Bill O'Grady, analyst with A.G. Edwards in St. Louis.
"I think it is unlikely that this will be one of the last builds given refineries are producing around 8.0 million barrel a day (of gasoline)," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.
Traders and analysts, however, were more unanimous on the future of heating oil prices, which are expected to lose strength sometime soon.
Traders have recently been scooping up large parcels of heating oil and putting them into storage ahead of winter to take advantage of a contango on NYMEX, and tanks are thus nearing full capacity.
For the week API reported distillate stocks up 905,000 barrels, putting inventories at 12.7 million barrels above year-ago levels.

"Heat continues to hold up very well because you've got a lot of it going into secondary storage. But one of these weeks, it's going to get backed up into primary storage and stocks will go up by 5 million barrels in one report," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil in Chicago.
